angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 20,553,761 km at 80.71 pc = 3.4 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 47431: distance 80.71 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.011), at which the luminosity and radius hold (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 80.71 +/- 0.888 pc; Gaia DR3 parallax 12.9055 +/- 0.1751 mas (same row, RUWE 2.27), 73.7 standard errors, is not used
radiusSource: Radius 29.544 solar radii from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 47431: radius 29.544 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 270.611 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.059) and temperature (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433): 20,553,761 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. No mass is measured, so GM is 0, the records' unpublished value. Temperature 4310 +/- 125 K from McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 47431: effective temperature 4310 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.066) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 47431: effective temperature 4310 +/- 125 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.066) (https://doi.org/10.1093/mnras/stx1433)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's measured spectrum (Pulkovo spectrophotometric catalogue, table 5 (320-1080 nm, 2.5 nm steps, 10 nm resolution, absolute flux in W m^-2 m^-1)) (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
